newsitem.title: COMOROS: Six alleged Comoran dissidents charged.
newsitem.headline: Six alleged Comoran dissidents charged.

text.p: Six youths were charged in the Indian Ocean Comoro Islands on Monday with belonging to a dissident group opposed to the government of President Mohamed Taki.
The six were arrested on Saturday. They denied being members of The Group of Resistance, which claimed responsibility early this year for setting several government offices ablaze.
The group also published leaflets calling on the islanders to use violence if necessary to topple Taki. It was blamed last week for anti-government messages daubed on houses.
The Group of Resistance remains shadowy and its leaders are unknown, officials said. It was not immediately known whether the six in court on Monday were kept in detention or freed pending trial.
Several people died and hundreds were arrested in Comoros in March after clashes between stone-throwing villagers and armed troops on Anjouan island.
The Comoros, which has had 17 coups and attempted coups since independence from France in 1975, has this year been swept by a series of strikes by civil servants demanding salary arrears.
